The full guide is on our site. A free 40-minute trial lesson will tell you more than any checklist.

slides.title: Is my child old enough to start the Qur’an?
There is no single right age.
slides.body: Readiness usually matters more than a birthday.

slides.title: Signs your child may be ready
items: Can focus on a short activity
Can repeat a short phrase clearly
Follows simple instructions from an adult who is not their parent
Shows curiosity about what you recite

slides.title: It is never too late to begin.
slides.body: Beginners aged 13 to 16 can often move through letters and early reading quickly.

When practice turns into arguments, it is tempting to become stricter or to stop asking. There is usually room between the two.

The full guide, reviewed by one of our teachers, is on our site.

#quranforkids #muslimparents #quranlearning #onlinequranclasses #hifz

slides.title: When your child says “I don’t want to practise”
It rarely means they dislike the Qur’an.
slides.body: They may be tired, frustrated, worried about mistakes, or resisting a routine that has become difficult.

slides.title: Ask what they are really refusing
items: A page that feels too difficult

slides.title: Keep the expectation. Reduce the conflict.
Gentle does not mean giving up.
slides.body: It means finding a calmer, more manageable way back.
slides.note: Guide reviewed by Foruhar Rahmani, Qur’an teacher

slides.title: Çocuğunuz “Kur’an çalışmak istemiyorum” dediğinde
Bu, çoğu zaman Kur’an’ı sevmediği anlamına gelmez.
slides.body: Yorgun, bunalmış ya da hata yapmaktan çekiniyor olabilir; belki de zorlaşan bir düzene direniyordur.

slides.title: Asıl neye itiraz ediyor?
Beklentiyi koruyun. Çatışmayı azaltın.
Yumuşak davranmak vazgeçmek değildir.
slides.body: Daha sakin ve sürdürülebilir bir dönüş yolu bulmaktır.

posts.caption:
Our name comes from this verse. Tarteel is recitation that is distinct and measured, and it is what we hope every child grows into.

#tarteel #quranforkids #tajweed #quranrecitation

slides.translation: “And recite the Qur’an with tarteel (in a distinct and measured tone).”
